summary: Republish shared ETA windows after claim-free corrections and preserve terminal metadata across rollback

replay.detail: ETA consumers advance by an independent window generation rather than claim cuts. A SQL-trigger-maintained terminal metadata backlog survives older writers draining the shared queues and is repaired before serving after re-upgrade.

schema.detail: Add a member-local terminal metadata backlog and an insert trigger on the existing pending queue. The generation uses the existing indexed mission-change projection; no canonical claims or public schema change.

rules.detail: Existing selected-attempt durations, person-held exclusion, newest-64 candidate bounds and quartiles are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Older writers retain the backlog trigger but do not clear its entries. The ETA wire shape is unchanged.

downtime.detail: The additive local projection initializes during normal store opening.

recovery.detail: Rollback leaves the additive backlog unused until re-upgrade; original claims remain unchanged.
